acceptance_evidence.reference: Closed event and status schemas plus deterministic fixtures cover exact create/rename/close, bounded write coalescing, PID reuse separated by start time, incomplete linkage rejection, watched/excluded path filtering, no-content privacy, not-entitled/not-permitted/unavailable states, dropped sequences, overload counts, bounded retry posture, and always-active non-exact fallback. Five contract tests validate every shape and explicitly reject an exact claim with missing file identity, unknown measurement, a preceding gap, and missed deadline.

discovered_risks: Live Endpoint Security activation and event receipt remain untestable without Apple entitlement, provisioning, signing identity, Full Disk Access, and an approved test host.
The system-extension transport's code-signing and application-group policy must be bound to actual identifiers during release packaging.
Exact attribution is event-local; any sequence discontinuity, stream restart, overload, or incomplete measurement opens a visible gap and forces downgrade.

evidence: All changes are inside the declared EndpointSecurity schemas, fixtures, contract tests, and provenance architecture document.
Schema-valid fixtures cover create, rename with destination, and close-backed coalesced writes with logical/allocated before, after, and delta values.
Process identity requires PID plus start time and file identity requires volume plus file ID; reused PID fixtures remain unequal identities.

Manual semantic checks require complete process/file linkage, complete non-unknown measurement, included scope, no preceding gap, deadline success, and the direct Endpoint Security method before exact is eligible.
Dropped-event and overload fixtures carry explicit gap and counts, forbid exact fallback confidence, keep snapshot/FSEvents active, and use bounded retry controls.

Path filtering deterministically excludes outside/excluded roots before emission, and contents, environment, arguments, and command line are absent from the event schema while privacy flags are constant false.
Not-entitled, not-permitted, unavailable, dropped, and overload statuses all retain active snapshot/FSEvents fallback and declare non-exact maximum confidence with limitations.
Five focused contract tests, all 88 repository tests, swift build, and git diff --check passed.
